title: Contract Based Verification of Non-functional Requirements for Embedded Automotive C Code
abstract: Abstract Code contracts provide a robust way to specify functional requirements of safety-critical software in embedded systems. For example, the ANSI/ISO C Specification Language (ACSL) can be used to specify the functional behavior of C code that is then formally verified by the Frama-C framework’s Wp plugin. However, non-functional requirements, such as restrictions on control flow and data flow, are also important for embedded systems safety. Untrusted code developed by subcontractors, junior developers, or generated by large language models can be verified by Wp but may nevertheless call unsafe functions or use uninitialized program variables. To address this problem, we constructed a set of general rules concerning requirements on control flow and data flow of C code in safety-critical embedded systems. Our rules are orthogonal to popular C rulesets such as MISRA-C and center on modules and their interactions through interfaces. To enable rule checking, we propose an interface specification contract language for C modules. We implemented a Frama-C plugin which takes as input a C module and its interface specification contract and checks our rules, ensuring, e.g., that only functions permitted by the contract are called by the module. We integrated our checker into a toolchain to enable specification and verification of module contracts and ACSL contracts for untrusted code. We report on two case studies on safety-critical C code using software from Scania trucks, where we defined module contracts and ACSL function contracts based on informal system requirements and verified them using our toolchain.

title: Shift-aware score transport for privacy auditing without retraining
abstract: Privacy auditing empirically assesses privacy leakage by using membership inference attacks to establish lower bounds on privacy loss. We consider an observational auditing setting in which the auditor cannot insert canaries, control data inclusion, or retrain the target model, and must instead rely on fixed sets of known members and non-members. This setting is relevant for large deployed models or when retraining is restricted by computational or access constraints. In this case, non-members available for auditing may differ in distribution from the training data, causing membership-inference scores to be skewed due to the distribution shift. We address this problem by estimating the counterfactual in-distribution non-member score distribution using the available out-of-distribution (OOD) non-members. Our proposed method learns the relationship between data representations and membership-inference scores from OOD non-members and transports it to the target covariate distribution. Because this transport may become unreliable under extrapolation or imperfect conditional invariance, we further introduce a conservative correction calibrated directly to the nominal transported privacy level. We construct controlled calibration tasks from the available non-member data to estimate how representation-space displacement inflates the audit, and use this estimate to correct the transport-induced audit error. Across multiple datasets with distribution shifts, our method yields substantially more stable privacy estimates while retaining tighter lower bounds than baselines.

title: Federated Differentially Private Optimization via Low-Rank Preconditioning
abstract: We consider differentially private (DP) optimization in the federated setting, where a DP estimate of the feature covariance matrix serves as a Hessian approximation for generalized linear models. Existing central DP methods for covariance estimation have communication cost that grows quadratically in the data dimension, while existing baselines with linear communication cost are only locally private and degrade as the number of clients increases. As a remedy, we propose a federated DP-PCA framework that achieves linear communication cost while providing central DP guarantees under secure aggregation. It consists of a DP rank selection step, a DP power method, and a noisy release of the covariance projected onto the selected low-dimensional subspace. We give error bounds for this covariance estimate and for the resulting low-communication preconditioned DP gradient descent. Empirically, our proposed DP optimization method matches a centralized baseline with quadratic communication cost at a fraction of the communication.

title: Dialect-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Arabic Question Answering: Measuring and Mitigating the Moroccan Darija–MSA Retrieval Gap
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems for Arabic are evaluated almost exclusively with Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) queries, although users write in dialect. We study this mismatch with a parallel benchmark of 200 questions written in both MSA and Moroccan Darija over 3,054 Arabic Wikipedia passages. Dialectal queries lower hybrid-retrieval Recall@1 from 0.755 to 0.620, and the loss reaches the answers: with five retrieved passages, answer correctness falls from 0.810 to 0.690, mostly through additional refusals; part of this loss persists even when the gold passage is supplied directly, so retrieval is the larger but not the only component. Rewriting Darija queries into MSA does not help. Zero-shot cross-encoder reranking raises dialectal Recall@1 to 0.800 (MSA: 0.755 unreranked, 0.875 reranked) and lets a single retrieved passage replace five unreranked passages with no loss larger than five percentage points and a 3.7-fold shorter prompt. Because dialectal queries are retrieved with lower confidence, gating the reranker on the retriever’s score margin concentrates its cost on them without any dialect detection, retaining 94% of the benefit while reranking about half of the queries. The findings hold under a human-validated LLM judge (Cohen’s κ=0.797), Holm correction and three prompt wordings, and replicate judge-free on a second, Darija-trained generator. We release the benchmark, corpus, code and all result files.

title: Formal Verification of the Heatseeker Technique for Detection of Code-Reuse Attacks
abstract: Abstract Formal verification of attack detection algorithms is essential to provide strong guarantees of correctness for security-critical protection mechanisms. Such guarantees are particularly important for signature-based defenses against code-reuse attacks, where undetected exploits can lead to the compromise of the entire system. These protection mechanisms provide interesting targets for formal verification, as they are typically implemented at the hardware or hardware/software interface. This paper presents a formal verification of a previously proposed signature-based detection mechanism, called heatseeker, designed to identify jump-oriented programming (JOP) attacks by monitoring control-flow transfers during program execution. We model both the detection algorithm and the target JOP attacks in C, and verify that the considered mechanism effectively detects any JOP attack using the bounded model checker . Thanks to the definition of suitable invariants on the algorithm’s internal state, bounded verification is sufficient to ensure the desired property for all executions. We present the formal model, the invariants, the proof methodology, and discuss the assumptions and limitations of the approach.

title: Same Luck, Different Choice: Twin-World Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning rewards a complete episode, yet the policy needs credit for every decision inside it. Counterfactual branching estimates this credit by re-running the episode after an alternative decision, but the branch draws its sampling noise independently of the factual episode, so the outcome difference mixes the effect of the decision with the luck of everything that follows. We observe that in agentic search the retriever, the corpus, and the grader are deterministic, so an episode is a deterministic function of the policy's decisions and its sampling noise. Twin worlds are therefore realizable: the same noise, a different decision. We introduce TWICE (TWIn-world Credit Estimation), which keys the Gumbel noise of every token by turn and line, rolls out counterfactual twins that inherit the factual episode's downstream noise, and turns their paired outcome differences into turn-level advantages for policy-gradient updates on actor-sampled trajectories; only the actor is deployed. Twin credit is unbiased for any coupling quality, its variance is that of an independent counterfactual scaled by $1-ρ$, where $ρ$ is the twins' outcome correlation, and under coupling the number of rollouts needed to resolve an advantage of size $Δ$ falls from $Θ(Δ^{-2})$ to $Θ(Δ^{-1})$. A square-root rule spends the twin budget where outcomes are predicted to disagree per unit cost. On seven question-answering benchmarks, TWICE improves the average exact match of GRPO by 5.3 and 4.5 points on Qwen2.5-3B and 7B, outperforms tree-search and counterfactual-branching baselines, and uses 68% fewer auxiliary tokens than VinePPO.

title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
abstract: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.

title: PYTHIA, a transferable machine learning framework for simultaneous defect and adsorption site optimization
abstract: Machine learning has permeated material optimization, providing high value. Nevertheless, its re- liance on a high number of samples limits its applicability to relatively explored material families. In this paper we extend the applicability of machine learning to novel and understudied materials through the PYTHIA (Probabilistic Yet Transferable Hierarchical Interaction Architecture) framework. Pythia utilizes two of the most powerful machine learning concepts, foundational models and transfer learning. We employ a complex foundational model trained on a large dataset of chemically similar molecules, on a target that is physically close to our prediction target. Then, we freeze the weights and perform subspace alignment with the use of a transformer layer and add uncertainty quantification with gaussian processes. These two layers can be trained on a limited dataset yet allow us to leverage the gained knowl- edge and the studied materials and complex architectures. The resulting model is used as a surrogate for a Bayesian Optimization scheme. title: A General-Purpose Dual-Path Interaction Framework for Multi-View Medical Image Segmentation: Alleviating Data Volume Dependency in Small-Sample Regimes
abstract: The performance of medical image segmentation depends on a large amount of annotated data, and most segmentation models experience a significant drop in performance in low-sample-size scenarios. Existing semi-supervised and weakly supervised methods rely on specific network architectures, while traditional multi-view-assisted segmentation methods require strictly paired samples, which limits their clinical applications. To address these issues, we propose DPIF, a general-purpose plug-and-play dual-path interaction framework compatible with arbitrary encoder-decoder segmentation networks, which leverages cross-view anatomical complementarity to reduce annotation reliance. DPIF first performs Sinkhorn optimal transport-based cross-view distribution alignment to establish global semantic correspondence without sample-level pairing. It then adopts conditional mutual information-guided feature decoupling to enable bidirectional knowledge transfer only within the shared semantic space, suppressing view-specific noise. Finally, persistent homology-based topological regularization encodes anatomical invariants as unsupervised priors to mitigate overfitting. Experiments were conducted using 24 baseline models on a private multicenter echocardiography dataset and two public datasets. The results show that DPIF-enhanced models outperform single-view baseline models when trained on comparable amounts of data. Notably, most dual-path variants trained on 40\% - 60\% of the data achieve performance comparable to that of single-view models trained on the full dataset. This demonstrates that DPIF provides a general-purpose and scalable solution for data-scarce multi-view medical image segmentation problems.

title: Local distinguishability of six bipartite orthogonal product states
abstract: It is necessary to investigate the local distinguishability of orthogonal quantum state sets, as their adoption in protocol design helps diminish quantum state transmission and cut operational costs. In this paper, we explore the local distinguishability of six orthogonal product states (OPSs) on any bipartite quantum system. We classify different sets of six bipartite OPSs into eight categories by using the vectors of the numbers of pairwise orthogonality relations, where any two states are orthogonal on only one subsystem within each set. We find that these eight categories contain a total of 78 distinct cases, all but five of which are perfectly distinguishable via local operations and classical communication (LOCC). Furthermore, we discuss the local distinguishability of those five distinct cases in detail. Our work explicitly characterizes the local distinguishability of six bipartite OPSs.

title: An Explainable Attention‐Driven EfficientNetB7 Framework for Early Detection of Head and Neck Cancer Using Digital Holographic Microscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a deep learning (DL) framework for head and neck cancer (HNC) detection using holographic imaging data. A self‐curated dataset of holographic and corresponding bright‐field images is used for comparative evaluation, demonstrating the novelty of the approach. The framework employs an EfficientNetB7 backbone integrated with a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) to enhance feature representation via channel and spatial attention mechanisms. To address class imbalance, class weighting and focal loss are applied to improve learning for minority classes. Experimental results demonstrated strong performance, achieving 96.93% validation accuracy, 97.80% test accuracy, and 99.31% area under the curve (AUC), outperforming bright‐field imaging data. The attention‐guided model improved classification performance by up to 12.72% over baseline models. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for accurate and early detection of HNC. Furthermore, explainability is incorporated using gradient‐weighted class activation mapping (Grad‐CAM) variants and local interpretable model‐agnostic explanations (LIME), providing qualitative visual insights into the model's decision‐making process, thereby facilitating its potential use in future computer‐aided decision support.

title: LACToS: Local Anomaly Detection via Conditional Typicality of Superpixels
abstract: Local anomaly detection is the task of identifying spatially confined anomalous or out-of-distribution (OOD) regions within an otherwise in-distribution (ID) image. Most existing methods are designed for a specific context, with a strong focus on industrial defect detection, where they achieve excellent performance on well-established benchmarks. However, we observe that these methods can exhibit significant performance drops in other contexts, especially when the inlier distribution is multimodal. To account for this inlier complexity, we propose LACToS, a principled local OOD detection method based on statistical typicality and made tractable through two innovations: (i) grouping pixels into superpixels and (ii) using a computationally efficient proxy to estimate typicality. We evaluate LACToS across three diverse applications spanning medical imaging, human faces, and X-ray security screening. LACToS performs more robustly than prior methods across these benchmarks. The code is released here: https://github.com/voilalab/LACToS.

title: GHz-rate all-fiber active polarization state analyzer for quantum protocols
abstract: Active selection of the measurement basis underpins quantum protocols including device-independent quantum key distribution, quantum teleportation with active feed-forward, and Bell tests. High-speed operation is crucial to minimize the latency between consecutive measurement choices, enabling faster protocol execution and higher achievable communication rates. Here, we demonstrate a GHz-rate all-fiber polarization state analyzer enabling active, trial-by-trial reconfiguration of the measurement basis, which we validate by performing a CHSH Bell test. The state analyzer is based on a fiber Sagnac interferometer incorporating a lithium niobate electro-optic phase modulator, built entirely using off-the-shelf fiber-optic components. Operating at a nominal repetition rate of 1 GHz, the system performs dynamic polarization measurements for the CHSH Bell test, achieving polarization visibilities up to 99% and a violation of $S = 2.6975 \pm 0.0005$, certifying entanglement at an unprecedented rate. Furthermore, the system demonstrates excellent long-term stability, preserving the Bell-inequality violation for more than 6 hours without realignment. These results establish the proposed state analyzer as a versatile, scalable platform for quantum communication protocols requiring fast, reconfigurable polarization-state measurements.

title: A multi-task learning approach for consumer sentiment classification and emotion detection via behavioral data
abstract: Sentiment analysis captures overall opinion polarity, but it often fails to reveal the key emotions that drive consumer behavior. The recognition of both sentiment and emotions provides crucial information to uncover underlying drivers of consumers behavior and brand loyalty. These important insights enable businesses to detect emerging issues, refine products and services, and personalize consumer experiences. This study proposes a multi-task approach that performs sentiment classification and emotion detection tasks based on consumer reviews and corresponding ratings. To this end, we propose Consumer Sentiment and Emotion Modeling ( COSMO-MT ), a deep learning-based multi-task model for sentiment classification and emotion detection. It begins with an input layer followed by embedding layers that provide sentiment-specific, emotion-specific, and shared embeddings from the input text. Each embedding is processed through shared layers consisting of CNN, BiLSTM, and attention mechanisms. Moreover, several auxiliary features are incorporated into the shared layers to provide explicit linguistic information. The outputs of the shared layers are then passed to task-specific layers for sentiment classification and emotion detection. Finally, corresponding dense and output layers generate predictions for both tasks. We evaluate the efficacy of the proposed COSMO-MT model on two publicly available datasets. It significantly outperforms existing studies and baseline methods.

title: An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks
abstract: Knowledge graph-to-text (KG-to-text) generation verbalizes a set of knowledge graph triples into fluent natural language. While fine-tuned encoder-decoder models have long been the standard approach, recent LLMs are becoming increasingly competitive. We benchmark recent LLMs against fine-tuned encoder-decoder models, using reference-based metrics and graph-grounded reference-free LLM-based evaluation validated against human annotations. We observed that recent LLMs substantially narrow, and in several settings close, the gap with fine-tuned models on reference-based metrics, while performing better on graph-grounded metrics. LLM-based evaluation scores show limited correlation with reference-based metrics, suggesting that the two approaches capture different aspects of generation quality. Graph-grounded evaluation reveals that prompted models produce fewer contradictions and triple omissions than fine-tuned models, and these errors increase more rapidly with graph size for fine-tuned models, highlighting differences between the two approaches that reference-based metrics may not fully capture.

title: Diagnosing the Explicit-to-Applied Theory of Mind Gap in LLMs
abstract: As large language models are deployed in high-stakes roles such as therapy, education, and personal assistance, their social cognition must be assessed reliably. Current Theory of Mind (ToM) benchmarks report aggregate scores that conflate two distinct competencies: explicit ToM (recognizing what someone believes) and applied ToM (using that belief to predict behavior). Building on this distinction, we investigate the gap and its recoverability using four structurally diverse benchmarks. Aggregate reporting obscures uneven competence: on SimpleToM, Llama-3.1-8B scores 51.5 percent overall while recognizing mental states at 99.4 percent and predicting behavior at only 28.9 percent. To assess recovery, we compare structured prompting, matched in-context learning, and our proposed Belief-State Test-Time Training (BSTTT), which adapts lightweight parameters on answered support questions through action reconstruction. Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and GPT-oss-20B, recovery depends on the model, task, and intervention. On SimpleToM, reminders combined with BSTTT improve Llama's behavior prediction by 40.8 percentage points; reminders account for most of the overall improvement, with BSTTT adding 1.3 to 5.5 points beyond reminders across models. Contextual examples often outperform weight updates, while BSTTT remains stronger in specific model-benchmark settings. Temporal belief tracking remains difficult despite partial recovery. These findings show that aggregate ToM scores can overstate applied competence while hiding performance recoverable through targeted assistance. We recommend decomposed reporting of explicit and applied accuracy alongside intervention comparisons that establish which failures are recoverable and under what conditions.

title: Synthetic data for open medical research: what practitioners should know
abstract: Publicly releasing research data is at the core of the open science principles. In medical research, however, this practice conflicts with confidentiality requirements for the collected data. One appealing solution to this dilemma is to release altered versions of these data instead of the original ones. Synthetic data are gaining increasing attention for such uses by clinicians, statisticians, and ethicists in the healthcare domain; yet, this interest is slow to materialize. One reason for that is a lack of familiarity among practitioners with synthetic data, in part explained by their abstract and technical nature. In this article, we address this need by reviewing, in a rigorous yet accessible way, the main ethical, technical, and logistical aspects of data synthesis that may be relevant to non-specialist practitioners who wish to engage with synthetic data in support of open research. In addition to the general principles for generating and evaluating synthetic data, this includes the current challenges that still hinder their democratization, as well as some research directions to overcome them.

title: Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona)
abstract: We propose a new regression method named Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) that directly uses samples to estimate the state and its derivatives at a query point, along with their admissible bounds, without long global training. By casting the values and derivatives at the query and neighbouring samples as latent variables in a constrained optimisation problem, the burden of long training loops becomes one of on-demand local solves. We establish Diona's theoretical properties including finite-sample coverage and, in the noiseless case, convergence to the true state and derivatives under dense sampling. In a nonlinear regression benchmark on six functions of three to eight dimensions, Diona was more accurate than a Gaussian process (GP) on noiseless data especially with denser data sets. Furthermore, as with GP, it produced uncertainty bounds that contained the true value at more than 95% of query points in four functions. Diona's time to a first prediction after a data set update was three to four orders of magnitude shorter than that of the GP, and two to three orders shorter than that of a neural network, which was more accurate but offers no uncertainty quantification. This low latency is paid for by on-demand predictions, so this latency advantage applies when relatively few predictions are needed between data updates.

title: Directing to Diversify: Multi-Directional Search for Automatic Heuristic Design
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong potential to automate heuristic design for NP-hard combinatorial optimization (CO) tasks without human intervention. Recent methods predominantly rely on evolutionary computation (EC) frameworks, where heuristic diversification is mainly induced through EC-like operators or downstream selection, while the direction of heuristic transformation remains largely unharnessed. In this paper, we propose a multi-directional Perturbation-Rewrite Search (PRS) framework for automatic heuristic design that factorizes heuristic transformation through directional search primitives at the generation level. Specifically, PRS operates on heuristic ideas through three complementary directions: expansion toward richer and more expressive designs, compression toward simpler and less specialized designs, and steering for fine-grained refinement, together enabling broader and more sustained exploration of diverse regions in the heuristic design space. PRS further organizes candidate exploration within a breadth-first search-based process with adaptive operator control, which ensures thorough candidate utilization and sustained exploration, and maintains strong search dynamics while preventing premature convergence. Extensive empirical results across diverse CO tasks show that PRS consistently discovers high-quality heuristics, demonstrating the effectiveness and generality of explicitly directional exploration design.

title: CHATBOT PANDUAN FITUR APLIKASI WAKTOO MENGGUNAKAN TF-IDF DAN SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE
abstract: Efisiensi layanan karyawan merupakan aspek penting dalam manajemen sumber daya manusia. Namun, keterbatasan jumlah personel sering menghambat penyampaian informasi dan panduan penggunaan aplikasi perusahaan kepada karyawan baru, khususnya mahasiswa magang. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan chatbot sebagai media pendamping dalam memberikan informasi terkait penggunaan aplikasi Waktoo HRM, meliputi presensi, manajemen tugas, dan kebijakan perusahaan. Dataset yang digunakan terdiri atas pattern, response, dan label intent yang disimpan pada database MongoDB. Sistem chatbot dibangun menggunakan Streamlit dengan pendekatan Natural Language Processing (NLP), memanfaatkan Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) sebagai metode ekstraksi fitur dan Support Vector Machine (SVM) melalui implementasi LinearSVC pada pustaka Scikit-Learn sebagai algoritma klasifikasi intent. Evaluasi model dilakukan menggunakan train-test split 80:20 serta Stratified 5-Fold Cross Validation pada data latih untuk mengukur konsistensi dan kemampuan generalisasi model. Kinerja model dievaluasi menggunakan metrik accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, dan confusion matrix. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan accuracy sebesar 84,44%, precision 85,69%, recall 84,44%, dan F1-score 84,01%. Selain itu, cross-validation menghasilkan rata-rata F1-score sebesar 0,87 dengan standar deviasi 0,02 yang menunjukkan performa model yang konsisten. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi TF-IDF dan SVM efektif dalam mengklasifikasikan intent pengguna pada chatbot Waktoo HRM.

evidence.abstract: Efisiensi layanan karyawan merupakan aspek penting dalam manajemen sumber daya manusia. Namun, keterbatasan jumlah personel sering menghambat penyampaian informasi dan panduan penggunaan aplikasi perusahaan kepada karyawan baru, khususnya mahasiswa magang. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan chatbot sebagai media pendamping dalam memberikan informasi terkait penggunaan aplikasi Waktoo HRM, meliputi presensi, manajemen tugas, dan kebijakan perusahaan. Dataset yang digunakan terdiri atas pattern, response, dan label intent yang disimpan pada database MongoDB. Sistem chatbot dibangun menggunakan Streamlit dengan pendekatan Natural Language Processing (NLP), memanfaatkan Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) sebagai metode ekstraksi fitur dan Support Vector Machine (SVM) melalui implementasi LinearSVC pada pustaka Scikit-Learn sebagai algoritma klasifikasi intent. Evaluasi model dilakukan menggunakan train-test split 80:20 serta Stratified 5-Fold Cross Validation pada data latih untuk mengukur konsistensi dan kemampuan generalisasi model. Kinerja model dievaluasi menggunakan metrik accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, dan confusion matrix. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan accuracy sebesar 84,44%, precision 85,69%, recall 84,44%, dan F1-score 84,01%. Selain itu, cross-validation menghasilkan rata-rata F1-score sebesar 0,87 dengan standar deviasi 0,02 yang menunjukkan performa model yang konsisten. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi TF-IDF dan SVM efektif dalam mengklasifikasikan intent pengguna pada chatbot Waktoo HRM.

title: Synthetic data for open medical research: current challenges and perspectives
abstract: Open science practices have many advocated benefits. At their core is the sharing of open data, especially open research data. Although their value is widely recognized, such data are rarely available in the healthcare domain. One of the main barriers to their dissemination is the fear of statistical disclosure by data custodians. Synthetic data represent a promising way to address this concern by altering the dependency of the released data on the original ones. Despite their intuitive appeal, synthetic data themselves come with many difficulties that have so far prevented their widespread adoption. In this article, we review the main ethical, technical, and logistical challenges associated with data synthesis for open medical research, and discuss some promising directions to overcome them. These current challenges and lines of research are placed in historical perspective and illustrated with several examples formalized within a unified statistical framework.

title: Nonparametric autoregressive estimation of probability distributions with parallel gradient boosting
abstract: Nonparametric estimation of joint probability distributions is a core problem in statistics, which is notoriously challenging with high-dimensional data. Such challenges also arise with conditional distribution estimation and have led to flexible algorithms that aim to tackle the ''curse of dimensionality'' by exploiting predictive structures of lower dimension than the ambient space. In this paper, we study the use of such conditional distribution estimators to estimate joint distributions by factorizing the latter in an ''autoregressive'' way. We show that for loss functions satisfying a subadditivity property, bounds on the convergence rate of an autoregressive estimator can be derived from bounds on the convergence rate of the conditional distribution estimators. These bounds relate the difficulty of estimating the joint distribution to that of estimating the most challenging factor in the autoregressive factorization. When the conditional estimators adapt to sparsity in their conditioning sets, we characterize this difficulty through variable elimination in an undirected dependence graph. This allows bounding the rates of convergence by quantities related to the sparsity of the graph, and provides an additional motivation for the autoregressive approach. We then evaluate the practical performance of an autoregressive estimator based on parallel gradient boosting, a flexible nonparametric method for estimating conditional distributions. The estimator demonstrates competitive estimation performance on various simulated and real datasets, even without optimizing the factorization order. Together, these results support nonparametric autoregressive estimation as a practical approach to flexible joint distribution estimation.

title: Harm Is Behavioural, Moderation Is Lexical: How Language and Culture Decide Whom Automated Safety Systems Protect and Whom They Silence
abstract: Content warning: this paper quotes slurs and hateful statements from published test suites; the racial slur among them is masked. Automated systems decide at scale which messages are harmful, and they decide unevenly. Classifiers label African American English as offensive up to twice as often as other English, the accounts of prominent drag queens can score as more toxic than those of white nationalists, and safety behaviour that holds in English collapses in low-resource languages. We argue that over-flagging and under-protection share one cause: deciding harm from vocabulary and surface form rather than from what a message does. We organise the evidence into seven failure modes and argue, as testable hypotheses, that harmful behaviours (a request for secrecy, a demand for payment, an attempt to isolate someone) travel across languages better than the words that express them. We propose an evaluation protocol that makes the gap between the best- and worst-served language communities a headline result, and show that the naive gap is inflated under equal service and that its usual bootstrap interval is unreliable. Applied to five open systems in eleven languages, from a keyword lexicon to two current multilingual guard models, the protocol finds that none reaches native-speaker accuracy at separating harmful function from harmless form (51 of 55 system-language pairs fall short); that greater capability raises discrimination in nine languages while leaving Arabic and romanised Hindi near chance, so the gap between the best- and worst-served languages grows with capability; that one system both over-flags and under-protects the same language most; and that a language a system reads worst can look the most fairly treated when only false positives are reported.

title: PENGEMBANGAN CHATBOT WHATSAPP BERBASIS DECISION TREE UNTUK OTOMATISASI INFORMASI PENDAFTARAN SANTRI BARU DI PESANTREN
abstract: Digital transformation int he Islamic boarding school environment has prompted the need for a system that can simplify the registration process for new students. This study aims to develop a WhatsApp-based chatbot using the Decision Tree (CART) algorithm as a solution for automating information services and registration forms at the Salafiyah Shirothul Fuqoha Islamic Boarding School Salafiyah Shirothul Fuqoha'. The development method used is a prototyping model with stages of needs analysis, interaction flow design, branching logic implementation, and testing. The chatbot is designed to guide prospective students in accessing information, filling in data, determining dormitoriesbased on program type, and calculating total costs by adjusting to the user's economic conditions. The system was evaluated using a confusion matrix for 25 menu interactions, resulting in an accuracy of 76%, precision of 89.47%, recall of 80.95%, and an F1-score of 85.05%. These results indicate that the Chatbot performs well in accurately responding to structured inputs and is suitable for use in supporting the efficiency of pesantren administration. However, further development is needed in terms of input validation and system scalability.

title: Diffusion-Based Synthesis of Complete 3D Biparametric Prostate MRI
abstract: Synthetic biparametric MRI (bpMRI) may help alleviate the limited availability of large and representative prostate MRI datasets for deep learning applications. In this work, we present a conditional 3D diffusion framework for anatomy-conditioned synthesis of complete prostate bpMRI from anatomical masks. The framework supports sequential synthesis, in which T2w and diffusion modalities are generated by separately trained models, and joint synthesis, in which all bpMRI modalities are generated simultaneously within a single model. Five configurations were trained using PI-CAI, FastMRI Prostate, and PROSTATEx datasets to investigate different conditioning schemes, target modalities, and synthesis strategies. Evaluation using distribution-based metrics, paired-image similarity, and qualitative assessment demonstrated the feasibility of both synthesis pathways. Joint synthesis achieved competitive distributional fidelity while generating complete bpMRI, whereas direct synthesis of ADC and computed high-b-value DWI outperformed their derivation from synthetic diffusion-weighted images.

title: Conflict-Aware Logit Adapters for Utility-Preserving Anti-Distillation
abstract: While reasoning traces improve model capability, they also provide supervision signals for downstream distillation. Initial efforts to mitigate this issue rely on decoding-time interventions, but they incur high inference overhead and can harm the teacher model's natural fluency. We propose Conflict-Aware Logit Adapters (CALA), a lightweight training-time defense. CALA attaches a small residual adapter to a frozen teacher model and trains only the adapter. A proxy student identifies positions where imitation is most sensitive, and the adapter perturbs the output distribution at these positions while remaining within high-probability regions. A conflict-aware optimization strategy balances anti-distillation and utility objectives, while regularization preserves the teacher's performance and fluency. At inference time, CALA incurs modest overhead and requires no auxiliary model. Experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that CALA substantially reduces successful student imitation while maintaining near-original teacher performance and generation quality. These results establish CALA as a practical and efficient alternative to decoding-time approaches.

title: Beyond Causal Masks: Auditing and Localizing Hidden Future-Token Leakage in Adaptive Sequence Models
abstract: Hidden future-token leakage can create false architectural gains: an autoregressive model may appear substantially better under teacher-forced evaluation while its free-running generation deteriorates. We investigate this failure in an adaptive residual-routing decoder whose sequence-level routing summary exposes prefix positions to future tokens despite a correct causal attention mask. An anomalous 24-layer checkpoint reduces validation loss from the baseline's 3.5958 to 1.4259, yet it fails a prefix-invariance audit and has substantially higher reference-model perplexity during generation. Layer-wise diagnostics and implementation inspection trace the violation to a full-sequence summary broadcast through the dynamic routing-query path. Two independently trained 12-layer causal repairs eliminate detectable leakage and return validation loss and reference perplexity to the control scale, removing the large apparent advantage. As diagnostic tools, we use the established prefix-invariance contract, maximum prefix-output discrepancy (LeakScore), complementary behavioral metrics, and layer-wise profiles. Supporting experiments cover six synthetic implementation pairs spanning five module families, clean pretrained controls, controlled fault injection, and cache consistency across numerical precisions. These results illustrate how hidden future-token access can produce misleading claims of architectural progress and why lower teacher-forced loss should be interpreted together with whole-model causal checks and free-running evaluation.

title: Algorithmic drift in generative adaptive learning
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence promises to democratize personalized tutoring, yet the longitudinal stability of adaptive systems remains under-theorized. Current ethical discourse focuses on static bias. This paper argues that a distinct threat lies in algorithmic drift: a feedback loop in which minor, demographically asymmetric observation errors compound over time into systemic inequities. We make three contributions. First, we formalize algorithmic drift as a coupled learner--tutor dynamical system. Second, we corroborate this theory with an agent-based Monte Carlo simulation in which either a transparent online tracker or an LSTM deep-knowledge-tracing network drives an IRT-based curriculum policy. Third, we introduce the temporal fairness stabilizer (TFS), a targeted intervention that periodically re-probes learner capability, and benchmark it against standard exploration baselines with explicit group-fairness metrics and replication-level inference. Within the modeled environment, TFS closes the achievement gap where generic exploration does not, and we characterize the conditions under which it succeeds. We separate what is established analytically, what is demonstrated in simulation, and what remains to be validated with real learners. Our results reframe algorithmic fairness in education as a temporal property of a closed loop rather than a deployment-time checkbox.

title: Jev-DLC: Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback
abstract: Individual preferences often become visible only after deployment, when a user accepts one decision or revokes it in favor of another. Jev-style typed interfaces make this feedback explicit by identifying the selected action and, under revocation, the decision it replaces. We study how these consequences persist across requests as Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback (Jev-DLC). Jev-DLC treats each correction as both evidence about a recurring action identity and a directed relation between the preferred and rejected choices. It preserves these signals in complementary bounded channels above a frozen scorer and combines their scores to shape the next decision. The method retains no raw interaction history, adds no scorer call, and performs no runtime language-model backward pass. We also introduce TCPA-Bench, a chronological suite that credits a correction only through its effect on later decisions. On TCPA-Repeat, Jev-DLC reaches 44.83% user-macro accuracy overall, 2.43 points above Recent-4 history replay. After at least two earlier feedback events, it reaches 56.07%, a 7.54-point margin over the strongest reported comparison at this depth. These results show how explicit typed corrections can become compact causal state for continual personalization.

title: ResGVC: Residual Coding for High-fidelity Generative Video Compression
abstract: Generative video compression (GVC) methods usually employ decoder-side diffusion models to denoise reconstructed signals based on generative priors. Besides, most of these methods perform denoising in latent space rather than directly in pixel domain. In this paper, we propose ResGVC, a residual coding framework for GVC that guides denoising toward original pictures by transmitting residual signals. ResGVC first encodes the original pictures within a learned video codec, and then decomposes the distortion between the codec reconstruction and the original pictures into a sequence of residual segments, where each residual segment is acquired at each denoising step. Residual segments can further be compressed by a novel residual codec with a diffusion transformer as an entropy model. Unlike prior methods, ResGVC introduces explicit source constraints throughout denoising rather than relying on decoder-side generation alone. The diffusion-based entropy model also enables more effective distribution modeling capability based on the powerful generative priors. Moreover, denoising directly in pixel space avoids the irreversible information loss caused by latent representation bottlenecks. Experimental results show that, compared with the previous state-of-the-art method, ResGVC achieves 63.7% and 83.8% BD-rate reductions in terms of LPIPS and PSNR, respectively, while also delivering superior visual quality.

title: UPI Fraud Detection Using Machine Learning with AI-Based Risk Score and Transaction Blocking
abstract: The rapid growth of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions has increased the need for effective methods to detect and prevent digital payment fraud. This project proposes a machine learning-based UPI fraud detection system that analyzes transaction details and identifies patterns that may indicate suspicious activity. Features such as transaction amount, time, frequency, recipient information, device details, and transaction history are used to assess each payment.The system applies machine learning to classify transactions and generate an AI-based risk score. It provides explanations for flagged transactions, such as unusually large payments, repeated transfers within a short period, or payments to unfamiliar recipients. Based on configurable risk thresholds, the system can approve low-risk transactions, send medium-risk transactions for review, and block high-risk transactions. A web-based dashboard displays transaction records, risk scores, alerts, explanations, and decision status for users and administrators.The proposed system aims to support faster fraud monitoring and provide a structured process for handling suspicious payments. Its performance depends on the quality and representativeness of the transaction data used for training and evaluation. The system is intended as a fraud prevention support tool, with final deployment and transaction blocking dependent on integration with authorized payment services

title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models
abstract: Metaphor is a crucial aspect of human cognition. As such, we would like to understand how it is represented in large language models (LLMs) and how it might be controlled. We use mechanistic interpretability techniques to identify causal subspaces in a range of LLMs covering different architectures and sizes. We show that we are able to steer output on classification tasks across different parts of speech. We are also able to steer output on generation tasks, indicating that these techniques can be used to control the metaphoricity of LLM output.

title: Multichoice Modeling: Exploring Decision Configuration Space under Uncertainty
abstract: Decision support has become sophisticated at exploring uncertainty, but much less so at representing the architecture of the decision itself. As a result, the decision space is often narrowed before uncertainty is analyzed, leaving interactions among choices and the effects of alternatives they imply largely invisible. This paper introduces multichoice modeling, a framework for making large decision configuration spaces explicit and computationally explorable under uncertainty. Drawing on the logic of rugged landscapes, we conceptualize such problems as contingent performance landscapes, where interdependent choices generate configuration-specific outcomes whose value changes across uncertain futures. The computational framework combines multidimensional decision and uncertainty spaces in a single simulation. Further, variance-based sensitivity analysis is used for identifying influential choices, and conditional distribution analysis for comparing configuration-specific performance profiles. We demonstrate the framework through three case studies: a manufacturing process upgrade, M&A strategy, and mortgage design. By contrasting conventional uncertainty-only analysis with multichoice modeling, the cases show how opening the decision configuration space can reveal unexpected complementarities, near-best configurations with different risk profiles, and strategies that were not apparent as alternatives at the outset.

We demonstrate the framework through three case studies: a manufacturing process upgrade, M&A strategy, and mortgage design. By contrasting conventional uncertainty-only analysis with multichoice modeling, the cases show how opening the decision configuration space can reveal unexpected complementarities, near-best configurations with different risk profiles, and strategies that were not apparent as alternatives at the outset.

title: From Prompt Rules to Golden Data Model: Production-Scale Generation of Personalized, Compliant Pharmaceutical Claims
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate domain-specific commercial & medical content (e.g., claims, statements, and promotional phrases) in regulated industries such as pharmaceuticals. However, ensuring its regulatory compliance, factual accuracy, and audience-specific personalization remains a major challenge. We report a production case study asking whether moving compliance and personalization signal from prompt-level rules into retrieval time structured context improves pharmaceutical claims generation, using Composer, a deployed internal tool built on a Golden Data Model (GDM) of 1,867 pharmaceutical claims spanning four products. The GDM integrates claim metadata, references, audience labels, material type, usage history, Match Text Variant (MTV) links, and a six dimension quality score (6C). Across six product-audience segments, the context pipeline improves intended indication (+29%), intended content type (+62%) and intended target audience (+67%), 6C quality score (+86%), and claim reuse (+34%). Production log analysis over the deployment period shows a 29.5% reduction in weekly API cost. We report this as descriptive deployment evidence. This work is a systems and data architecture contribution: it shows that in a regulated, high-stakes domain, restructuring claim data for retrieval-time filtering is a more scalable lever than expanding prompt-level rules, and documents the engineering path data cleaning, graph linking, and quality scoring.

title: CANNBot-CAKE: Collaborative Agentic Kernel Evolution for Ascend NPU
abstract: Efficient custom operators are essential for modern deep learning workloads, yet developing high-performance kernels for Ascend NPUs remains slow, expert-intensive, and difficult to automate. Although AI agents now approach expert performance on GPU kernel benchmarks, current models remain less capable of generating AscendC kernels for NPUs, potentially reflecting the relative scarcity of relevant training data. We thus present CAKE, a CANN-native system for deployable custom operators that combines adaptive multi-DSL routing, separate Generation and Evolution modes, and reviewed knowledge reuse through CAKE Book and a Self-Evolving Agent. On 53 CANN-Bench v1.1 operators on Ascend 950PR, CAKE's aggregated results achieve $100\%$ case pass rate on the standard set (1,060/1,060) and $98.28\%$ on the hidden set (4,167/4,240), with an overall mean score of 78.63 out of 100 and an average performance speedup of $1.334\times$ over the baseline. Evolution then pushes correct operators further: EngramGateFusion cuts aggregate device time by $46.6\%$ over 20 rounds and roughly halves the mean roofline gap. These results offer a practical path toward closing Ascend's AI-for-kernel capability gap.

title: Utjecaj generativne umjetne inteligencije na digitalnu autentičnost i povjerenje u online komunikaciji
abstract: Generativna umjetna inteligencija mijenja uvjete u kojima korisnici procjenjuju podrijetlo digitalnih poruka, vjerodostojnost informacija i pouzdanost njihovih pošiljatelja. Cilj je rada kritički razmotriti odnos između sudjelovanja umjetne inteligencije u stvaranju sadržaja, percipirane autentičnosti i povjerenja u online komunikaciji. Primjenjuje se kritički narativni pregled odabranih istraživanja, uz konceptualnu sintezu nalaza o AI autorstvu, označavanju sadržaja i sintetičkim komunikatorima. Razlikuju se empirijski nalazi iz tržišne komunikacije i šire implikacije koje tek treba provjeriti u drugim komunikacijskim okružjima. Analiza pokazuje da se autentičnost ne može svesti na ljudsko podrijetlo poruke, niti se vjerodostojnost može poistovjetiti s njezinom stvarnom točnošću. Negativne reakcije na AI autorstvo ovise o očekivanom ljudskom doprinosu, vrsti poruke i načinu predstavljanja komunikatora. Transparentnost istodobno omogućuje informiranu procjenu i može izazvati nepovoljnije vrednovanje sadržaja. Kao doprinos predlaže se konceptualni okvir provjerljivoga povjerenja koji povezuje podrijetlo sadržaja, obrazloženost tvrdnji, uredničku odgovornost i mogućnost ispravka. Okvir je analitički prijedlog, a ne empirijski potvrđen model. Zaključuje se da odgovorna online komunikacija zahtijeva više od oznake o uporabi umjetne inteligencije: korisniku treba omogućiti procjenu dokaza i utvrđivanje odgovornoga pošiljatelja. Razmatraju se ograničenja postojećih istraživanja te implikacije za informacijsku i AI pismenost.

title: Towards User Simulators That Stay On Task And Still Sound Natural
abstract: Users increasingly rely on AI systems for extended, multi-turn tasks, yet evidence indicates that LLM-based system performance degrades over prolonged interaction. To evaluate and improve AI assistants in such settings, we need user simulators that faithfully follow complex user intents while exhibiting realistic conversational behavior. Existing approaches manifest a trade-off: prompted assistants can follow complex user intents but lack behavioral fidelity, while specialized user simulators better approximate conversational behavior but struggle to remain faithful to complex intents. In this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) recipe that jointly rewards task intent adherence and behavioral naturalness. A crucial contribution of the method is operationalizing naturalness with a lightweight discriminator trained in an alternating, adversarial loop with the user simulator. We release the resulting model, UserLM-2.0, which produces valid simulated conversations (i.e., meeting both task-faithfulness and naturalness criteria) 46.2% of the time, over three times the rate of the strongest prior user simulator (14.1%).

title: NN-Based Transistor Modeling for Ultra-Fast SPICE Simulation and Standard Cell Library Characterization
abstract: Neural network (NN)-based transistor models have proven to be a promising solution to accelerate device modeling. Although these models demonstrated remarkable speedup in circuit simulations, they were not rigorously tested in complex tasks within standard EDA tool flows for chip design, which require very high transistor model precision to provide accurate results and converge properly. To investigate their full potential and promise, we develop NN-based transistor models that accurately predict the drain current and various charges for a 3nm nanosheet, and employ the models for a standard cell library characterization. This enables us to evaluate the accuracy and speedup under a very wide range of SPICE simulations, benchmarking our models against an industry-standard implementation. Since standard cell library characterization involves thousands of SPICE simulations, it serves as a great benchmark for transistor model quality and consistency. To further evaluate model accuracy, we also perform analog- and digital-level simulations for various complex circuits. Our experiments reveal that NN-based models are a valid alternative to existing transistor compact models, capable of producing accurate delay and power estimates with a much higher speed and convergence time compared to the conventional Verilog-A-based industry-standard (BSIM-CMG) transistor compact model. Our NNs achieve sub-0.11% and 0.76% errors for delay and total power evaluation on a wide range of circuits, while taking up to 8 times less time during the standard cell library characterization. Additionally, we provide comprehensive information and guidance on NN accuracy, unveiling the relationship between NN size and its effect on circuit simulation precision.

title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
abstract: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of centralized coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff dependencies. A prop legend and pot ingredient-count indicators provide explicit visual cues, while grid-based destinations support spatial grounding. The evaluation compares four VLMs on all 20 maps, measuring task score, order completion, delivery precision, action acceptance rate, and model API expenditure. A memory ablation on the same 20 maps examines the effect of a shared, self-authored notebook while retaining six-response action history in both conditions. The strongest evaluated model, \texttt{gpt-6-astra}, achieves 26.2\% mean order completion. Notebook memory has mixed score effects across models, with positive mean differences for Claude and Qwen and negative differences for GPT and Gemini.

title: Chunk Recomputation under Real Document Revisions: Measuring Update Cost and Retrieval Quality of Fixed, Recursive, and Content-Defined Chunking
abstract: Chunking strategies for retrieval-augmented generation are almost always evaluated on a static snapshot, yet the documents underlying a knowledge base continue to change. Because chunks are embedded independently, a boundary that moves after an edit forces unchanged text to be re-embedded. We measure this update cost on 120 pairs of adjacent Chinese and English Wikipedia revisions for three stateless chunkers (non-overlapping fixed-size, recursive paragraph-first, and content-defined chunking) under a strict byte-identical reuse rule and a frozen dense encoder. On the 116-article common-success pool, with frozen, length-calibrated parameters, fixed-size chunking recomputes 57-68% of its full new-version embedding-input workload, recursive chunking 38-56%, and content-defined chunking 43-54% (it failed on 4 of 62 Chinese articles), while at these parameters mean evidence recall under a fixed 2048-token retrieval budget differs by less than two percentage points within either language. A cost-only parameter grid shows that the ranking of the two content-aware chunkers changes with chunk-length settings, whereas non-overlapping fixed-size chunking has the highest recomputation cost in every length-matched condition. Controlled edits and a verbatim-presence diagnostic support boundary drift as one contributor to recomputation of text already present in the previous version. Update cost is therefore a substantial, parameter-sensitive dimension that static retrieval evaluations do not expose and that should be reported alongside retrieval quality.

title: Analisis Sentimen Program Magang Generasi Bertalenta Badan Usaha Milik Negara (MAGENTA BUMN) di Media Sosial X Menggunakan Word2Vec dan Support Vector Machine (SVM)
abstract: The State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) Talent Generation Internship Program (Magenta BUMN) is a human resource development program managed by the Indonesian Human Capital Forum (FHCI) that has attracted considerable public attention on the social media platform X. The high volume of unstructured public opinions makes manual program evaluation challenging. This study aims to measure the model's accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score; evaluate the effectiveness of combining the Word2Vec Skip-gram architecture with a Linear-kernel Support Vector Machine (SVM) to classify public sentiment toward Magenta BUMN; and identify the dominant aspects of positive and negative sentiment. The dataset consists of 664 Indonesian-language tweets collected between January 2023 and November 2025. The data underwent six preprocessing stages and were evaluated using 18 parameter combinations involving variations in data-splitting ratios, vector size, and window size. The best performance was achieved with an 80:20 data-splitting ratio, a vector size of 300, and a window size of 7, yielding an accuracy of 80.45%, precision of 78.46%, recall of 80.95%, and an F1-score of 79.69%. The average cosine similarity of 0.8991 indicates that the model effectively captures contextual relationships between words within the Magenta BUMN domain. Positive sentiment is predominantly associated with career development and financial compensation, whereas negative sentiment primarily concerns selection transparency and technical issues with the platform.

title: Piano2Pop: Expanding Piano Demos into Pop Productions Without Aligned Supervision
abstract: We introduce Piano2Pop, a music-expansion task that transforms piano MIDI into instrumental pop productions. Enabled by recent advances in music generation and polyphonic music transcription, our pseudo-supervised approach conditions a pretrained flow-matching model on piano rolls without aligned piano-pop supervision. We train on synthetic piano-instrumental pairs derived from pop recordings, comparing pair-free transcription, including function-selective (FST) and register-density (RDA) augmentations, with a pair-supervised piano-cover generator as pseudo-demo sources. On 476 testing real-world piano-cover/pop pairs, the pair-supervised approach achieves the best Frechet Audio Distance, Accompaniment Prompt Adherence, and spectral shape on real-piano inputs, while FST mitigates piano-heavy outputs in pair-free training and remains a promising alternative. All fine-tuned systems significantly outperform the zero-shot baselines, which suggests a role for task-specific modeling.

title: Mostly Reading: What Open-Book Scores Measure in Document-Level LoRA Adapters
abstract: Single-document LoRA adapters have been proposed as units of knowledge to be merged and retrieved; yet open-book scoring, with the document in the prompt, can credit a document's own adapter (its specialist) for reading that document as readily as for holding it. Training one adapter for each of 150 Wikipedia articles on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, we find that open-book scores mostly measure a reading behaviour every adapter shares: a random adapter trained on another document recovers 82 % of the specialist's open-book advantage over the base model but only 2 % of its advantage on a cloze probe that asks for the same document's facts without providing the source text, a share we cannot distinguish from zero. Content does reach the weights, since the specialists beat the base model in cloze recall by 0.094, and the geometry of their updates follows the documents they read; yet, in a test of 30 queries, adapters chosen by weight-space proximity or text embedding are not distinguishable from random ones on either probe, although that test cannot exclude an advantage of about four fifths of what a query's own adapter gains over a random one. At 16 documents or more, correctly scaled merges recover 87 % to 89 % of the specialists' open-book advantage but only 12 % to 16 % of their cloze advantage, with intervals that run from below zero to at most 32 %, against 94 % for joint training.We also report four silent errors, each of which produced a clean, wrong result.

title: FairFRESH: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Fair and Explainable Household Food Recommendation
abstract: Recommender systems typically serve one user at a time. However, in households, members share a finite pantry and follow different dietary rules, making independent recommendations prone to resource conflicts and dietary violations. We formulate household food recommendation as constrained fair division and present FairFRESH, a neuro-symbolic framework that learns per-member utilities, allocates foods under explicit welfare objectives, enforces dietary rules through a deterministic filter, and explains recommendations using Shapley and Banzhaf attributions. Theoretically, we show that no finite penalty guarantees compliance near a dietary-rule threshold, establish approximation guarantees for greedy allocation under utilitarian and smoothed Nash objectives in the stock-free model before filtering, and characterize the scale invariance of Nash welfare. We also use the minimax theorem to analyze rotating shared meals. On NHANES-derived data, the learned utility model achieves Recall@20 of 0.293, outperforming five learned recommenders (at most 0.244) but not a previous-day repetition heuristic (0.321). On held-out four-person households, Nash allocation reduces Gini disparity by 42% relative to conflict resolution while improving Recall@20 from 0.180 to 0.197. It comes within 2% of an upper bound on the smoothed Nash optimum, and rescaling one member's utilities changes at most 1.5% of assignments. All recommendations satisfy the encoded dietary rules, while attribution scores correlate with utility loss upon component removal (r = 0.76). In simulation, shared meals reduce pantry use by about one-third, and weekly rotation increases the worst-off member's utility by 38% over the best fixed meal.

title: XALIGN: A Human-centric Visual Analytics Approach to Understanding AI Explanations
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) methods are usually evaluated for technical properties such as faithfulness and robustness. In high-stakes application domains, experts also need to check model predictions against established knowledge. Different explanation methods often disagree, and this disagreement is hard to see when each method is inspected separately. We propose XALIGN, a visual analytics workflow and interface that shows rule-based explanations and several feature attribution methods (TreeSHAP, KernelSHAP, and LIME) side by side for the same Random Forest model. Agreements and contradictions between the methods become visible signals that users can explore and compare with domain knowledge. We apply XALIGN in two case studies: the German Credit dataset and a meteorological dataset, in which events derived from ICON model output and Cloudnet observations are classified. In both, the views reveal discrepancies between the rule-based explanation and the attribution methods that a single method would not show. In an expert evaluation with three specialists, participants found XALIGN useful for identifying influential features and for avoiding over-trust in predictions. Linking rules to attributions was harder for the participant without an XAI background.

title: “Pharos Night: Crown Pursuit”: An AI-Native Deck-Building and Tactical Arena Game Design Based on Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: With advancements in generative AI technology, an increasing number of researchers have begun exploring AI-native games in which gameplay rules are directly driven by generative AI. This paper presents "Pharos Night: Crown Pursuit," an AI-native deck-building and tactical arena game based on a multi-agent system. The game uses large language models to generate materials and cards, support NPC decision-making, and mediate natural-language interactions. During play, players collect materials, describe desired card effects in natural language, and choose whether to negotiate or fight with NPCs in the arena. To constrain model-generated outcomes, the system parses responses as structured JSON, constructs card effects from predefined mechanics, and maps qualitative effect levels to designer-specified numerical values. A small-scale playtest with 13 participants suggests that the system can provide strategically meaningful and engaging AI-driven gameplay, while also revealing challenges related to predictability, transparency, and player control. This work demonstrates the potential of multi-agent generative AI systems for creating more emergent digital game experiences.

title: Agent Behavior Reverse Engineering
abstract: Agent behavior reverse engineering asks what an agent has done, based on theactions it has taken. In its simplest form, the answer is an instruction or promptthat describes the task carried out by those actions. The usual direction is to givean agent a task and let it act; here, the direction is reversed, from actions back to atask. This paper argues that this problem deserves attention as a research direction.It also extends the idea to multi-agent systems, where the aim is to understandwhat each agent did and what they accomplished together. The main motivation issafety: understanding actual behavior can help determine whether an agent carriedout a harmful task. For hypothetical future agents with self-awareness, this abilitycould also help people understand the activities those agents choose for themselvesand their consequences. This paper explains the idea, gives simple examples, andoutlines ways to begin studying it.

title: Evaluation of Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Software Ensembles for Hippocampal Segmentation
abstract: Accurate hippocampal segmentation can be a useful tool for diagnosing and monitoring neurological conditions such as Alzheimer's disease and epilepsy. While numerous automated segmentation methods exist, their clinical adoption remains limited. Reliable uncertainty assessment can enhance trust and facilitate clinical translation. This study evaluates ensembles of five heterogeneous hippocampal segmentation methods - InnerEye, ASHS, FastSurfer, HippoSeg, and FreeSurfer - across two dementia datasets and one epilepsy dataset. The sub-ensemble containing InnerEye, FastSurfer, and HippoSeg emerged as both accurate and efficient, highlighting the feasibility of balancing computational cost and performance. Additionally, ensemble-derived uncertainty quantification with sample variance, mutual information, and predictive entropy is shown to reduce inaccurate segmentations by flagging low-confidence cases, potentially providing a mechanism for automatically escalating ambiguous cases for expert assessment. Lastly, this study explores the downstream clinical utility of ensemble-derived uncertainty, finding a significant correlation with motion artefact severity and a modest contribution to Alzheimer's disease classification.

title: Multi-Tool Selection for Robotic Systems: Comparing Semantic Retrieval and LLM
abstract: Natural-language interfaces allow users to command robotic systems without interacting directly with mission planners or robotics middleware. Their reliable use depends on robot tool routing, defined here as the selection of the smallest complete subset of predefined executable capabilities required to satisfy a request. This task is particularly difficult for compound instructions, where incomplete selection may omit necessary sensing or monitoring capabilities, while excessive selection may expose irrelevant tools. We compare four routing strategies: three progressively refined ChromaDB-based methods - fixed-threshold retrieval, relative-distance retrieval, and clause-aware aggregated retrieval - and a cloud-hosted 120-billion-parameter language-model baseline. The methods are evaluated on 164 manually annotated prompts organised into three complexity levels, from direct single-tool requests to compound requests requiring at least three tools. Using exact-match accuracy, completeness, precision, a completeness-weighted composite score, and routing latency, CDB-v3 achieves the best macro-average score among the retrieval-only methods, with 0.7822, compared with 0.8869 for the large-model baseline. Although the LLM provides higher routing quality, CDB-v3 exhibits substantially lower latency and can be deployed locally without requiring cloud connectivity. These results identify a quality-latency trade-off between direct large-model selection and clause-aware semantic retrieval for privacy-sensitive, connectivity-constrained, and resource-constrained robotic systems.

title: Generative AI and Copyrightability in the United States: Human Authorship, Creative Control, and AI-Assisted Works
abstract: The U.S. Copyright Office has released its report Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 2: Copyrightability. This paper explores the copyrightability of AI-generated and AI-assisted works in the United States, focusing on that report and on the jurisprudence of human authorship. It examines the constitutional and statutory bases of human authorship, the importance of Burrow-Giles, Feist, Community for Creative Non-Violence v. Reid and Thaler v. Perlmutter, and how the Copyright Office has dealt with prompting, human-authored inputs, selection, arrangement, modification and the assistive use of AI. The paper shows that the United States has adopted a case-by-case approach: the use of AI as a tool does not defeat protection, but copyright extends only to expression created by a human author and not to material generated by AI itself. Under current technology, prompts alone do not generally provide sufficient control, but human expression that is perceptible in the output, creative selection and arrangement, and meaningful modification can be protected. The paper sets out the strengths and weaknesses of this approach and suggests more explicit registration, evidentiary and guidance practices, while maintaining the human-authorship requirement.

title: Structure-preserving reduced-order models of thin panels in supersonic and hypersonic flow
abstract: We build structure-preserving reduced-order models for both challenge problems of the AePW-4 High-Speed Working Group. They are a clamped thin panel at Mach 1.92 (RC-19) and a cantilever plate at Mach 5.85 (HyMAX). The published data for each case hold no time-resolved response and no repeated runs. The physics must therefore be carried by the form of the model. One construction gives two models per problem. A Ritz-Galerkin reference model describes the plate. A learned model keeps the reference model's exact potential, fits the remaining generalized forces, and trains only a dissipation that cannot add energy. Its energy balance holds for any weights by construction. On the trained model the worst relative residual is 2.2e-15. On RC-19, shock relations predict a pressure ratio of 1.521 across the panel. Pressure-sensitive paint measured the same value. Thirty runs of the learned model place the mean dominant frequency within 1.0% of the measured 236 Hz. At one periodic and one chaotic condition, the learned model reproduces the response regime of a published reduced-order model in all sixteen runs. It does so without that model's 113 Hz spectral peak, which the measurements do not show. Measured displacements can also correct the chaotic response through one more force that respects the energy balance. We tested this on synthetic data at the experiment's 5 kHz sampling rate. The state error is 1.25% of the panel thickness without noise and 3.5% with 10 micrometers of noise. On HyMAX the learned model follows the reference model's trailing-edge displacement for 65 ms with a relative error of 3.7%. These results show that a model whose structure carries the physics can match measured flutter behavior when the available data cannot train it.

title: Evaluating Artificial Wisdom (AW): A Trajectory-Based Framework for Context-Sensitive Decision Regulation
abstract: Capability benchmarks measure what large language models can do, but not whether their recommendations remain appropriate as decision conditions change. This paper proposes a trajectory-based measurement framework and prospective validation protocol for artificial wisdom, defined behaviorally as context-sensitive regulation of judgment. Versioned reference specifications determine admissible responses and transition materiality before evaluation. Seven stage-level criteria assess judgment under current conditions, while two transition components assess material-update adequacy and commitment-preserving stability. Stability requires prior adequacy; switching within registered commitment classes is permitted, and persistent error earns no stability credit. A nine-component profile is primary, with a secondary bottleneck score and separate critical-failure reporting. Three simplified simulations examine precision, bottleneck estimation, and sensitivity to model-family count. A single-criterion simulation met its precision criteria at 24 scenarios per domain. Near a bottleneck tie, the estimated minimum had a downward bias of 0.55 points at that size. A simplified incremental-prediction simulation detected a Brier improvement of 0.027 with probabilities of .508 and .742 using eight and twelve families, respectively; it does not establish power for the operational protocol. An exploratory predecessor-rubric study comprising 71 evaluation records illustrates aggregation sensitivity but does not validate the proposed instrument. The twelve-family target remains provisional pending feasibility assessment and calibration of the complete analysis. Whether the profile predicts independent decision outcomes beyond capability remains an open empirical question.
